content.title: About
content.content: Broccoli slaw salad is a fresh mix of thinly shredded broccoli, carrots, red cabbage and onion, tossed in a light vinaigrette made with oil, vinegar, mustard and honey. It offers a crisp texture, a mild bite and a subtle sweet note.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli is rich in vitamins C, K and folate, as well as glucosinolates with antioxidant properties.
The term “slaw” comes from the English word for shredded cabbage, referring to finely sliced vegetables.
The salad is often served as a side to barbecue, fish or chicken because its bright flavor refreshes heavier dishes.
It can be prepared ahead of time – add the dressing just before serving to keep the vegetables crunchy.
Some recipes replace regular vinegar with rice or apple cider vinegar for a milder tang.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis, promoting healthy skin.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Fiber from broccoli and cabbage improves digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: The salad is low in calories, making it a great option for weight management.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Glucosinolates and carotenoids help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium in broccoli contribute to normal blood pressure.

items.title: Allergy to cruciferous vegetables
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to broccoli or cabbage.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Cruciferous vegetables can cause increased gas in sensitive people.

items.title: Possible pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic produce, rinse vegetables thoroughly to reduce residue.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a standalone dish or side. Enhance it with nuts, pumpkin seeds, dried fruit, or toasted tofu for extra protein.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Store the dressing separately to maintain crunch.

content.title: About
content.content: A cake or cupcake with zucchini is a baked good that incorporates grated zucchini, giving it moisture, a subtle flavor, and an extra serving of vegetables. These treats can be sweet or lightly spiced and are often topped with frosting, nuts, or berries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Zucchini is over 90 % water, so adding it to batter makes the cupcake extra moist.
The trend of zucchini cupcakes began in the United States in the 1970s as a way to use surplus summer vegetables.
Batter with zucchini often replaces part of the flour with whole‑grain flour, boosting nutritional value.
Zucchini is rich in vitamin C and potassium, making the cupcake a healthier dessert option.
Vegetarians and vegans frequently use plant‑based egg substitutes in zucchini cupcake recipes.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and minerals
items.content: Zucchini provides vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium, and magnesium, which support immune function and heart health.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: Sweetness is achieved with modest sugar, while moisture comes from the vegetable, resulting in a healthier treat.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from zucchini aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Beta‑carotene and lutein in zucchini help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Suitable for diet plans
items.content: The low calorie density of zucchini allows the cupcake to fit into moderate‑calorie diets.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: The cupcake may contain nuts, dairy, or eggs, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Despite low added sugar, the cupcake still contains carbohydrates, important for people with diabetes.

items.title: Potential food toxins
items.content: Raw zucchini can contain cucurbitacin, but it is destroyed during cooking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the zucchini cupcake as a standalone dessert, or serve it with yogurt, cottage cheese, or a berry sauce. It slices easily into portions and keeps well refrigerated.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cupcake in an airtight container at 0‑4 °C for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in freezer‑safe bags for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Raspberries, frozen are berries of the raspberry plant (Rubus idaeus) harvested at peak ripeness and quickly frozen to preserve flavor, aroma, and nutrients. The berries are small, bright red, and have a characteristic sweet‑tart taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Raspberries belong to the Rosaceae family and are close relatives of blueberries and blackberries.
Freezing occurs within hours of harvest, retaining over 90 % of vitamin C.
Antioxidant levels in frozen raspberries remain almost unchanged compared with fresh fruit.
Raspberries are used in sauces, desserts, smoothies, and baked goods.
In Russia, raspberries are cultivated in northern regions where the climate is favorable.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Raspberries contain anthocyanins and vitamin C, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in berries promotes regular bowel movements and enhances satiety.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is important for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: 100 g of frozen raspberries provide about 50 kcal, making them a good choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Raspberries provide manganese, magnesium, and iron, essential for metabolic processes.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to raspberries.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although low in calories, raspberries contain natural sugars that should be considered by people with diabetes.

items.title: Freezing quality
items.content: Improper storage can lead to ice crystal formation and texture loss.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raspberries can be added to smoothies, yogurt, oatmeal, baked goods, sauces, or enjoyed straight from the freezer as a cold snack. They do not need to be thawed unless a softer texture is desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store frozen raspberries in an airtight bag or container at –18 °C. Once thawed, consume within 1–2 days and do not refreeze.

content.title: About
content.content: A blend of vodka and an energy drink combines strong spirit with caffeine, taurine and other stimulants. It is often served as a shot or mixed cocktail, delivering a quick surge of energy and a mild buzz.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The alcohol‑caffeine combo can heighten the feeling of alertness while the body is actually being depressed by alcohol.
Some countries restrict the sale of ready‑made vodka‑energy mixes because of health concerns.
Energy drinks frequently contain B‑vitamins that may offset minor deficiencies but do not neutralize alcohol effects.
The popularity of these mixes surged in the early 2000s alongside club culture.

items.title: Improved focus
items.content: Caffeine can temporarily boost attention and reaction time, which some perceive as an “energy boost.”

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Energy drinks are often fortified with B6 and B12, vitamins involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: Alcohol‑stimulant interaction
items.content: Caffeine may mask the feeling of intoxication, leading to higher alcohol consumption and increased risk of poisoning.

items.title: Cardiovascular strain
items.content: Combining alcohol with high caffeine doses can cause rapid heart rate, elevated blood pressure, and arrhythmias.

items.title: Sleep disruption
items.content: Energy drinks contain significant sugar and stimulants, which can result in insomnia.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some ingredients in energy drinks (taurine, glucuronolactone) may cause individual intolerance.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: The blend is usually served in small portions (30–50 ml) as a shot or mixed cocktail. It is not recommended to combine it with other alcoholic beverages or consume large quantities.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dark place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, it is best consumed within 1–2 weeks to preserve the flavor and energy‑drink properties.

content.title: About
content.content: Waffle NFS is a crisp, airy snack made from whole‑grain flour, eggs, milk and a modest amount of sugar. It is popular as a quick bite and is often served with fruit, berries or a drizzle of cream.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Waffles originated in medieval Europe and were originally cooked over an open fire.
The classic waffle pattern of square pockets helps hold syrup and toppings.
Waffle NFS uses whole‑grain flour, increasing fiber content compared with standard waffles.
Waffles are a common breakfast item in North America and Europe.
There are many batter variations: classic, gluten‑free, vegan and protein‑enriched.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Whole‑grain flour provides a slow‑release source of energy, helping you feel fuller longer.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Eggs and milk supply a complete set of essential amino acids.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: The batter supplies thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain flour adds fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Waffle NFS is cooked with a small amount of oil, making it a lighter option.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The product contains wheat, so it should be avoided by people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Milk and egg allergy
items.content: Waffles contain dairy and eggs, which can trigger reactions in allergic individuals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although moderate, frequent consumption may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Waffles can raise blood sugar quickly, especially when eaten without protein or fat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Waffle NFS warm, drizzled with maple syrup, berry sauce, or sprinkled with nuts. It pairs well with yogurt, cottage cheese, fresh fruit, or avocado for a more balanced meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked waffles in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Reheat in a toaster or microwave before serving.
